bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Net cash in hand moved from ₹31.6 Cr (FY22) to a peak of ₹52.4 Cr (FY23), settling at ₹45.5 Cr in Q1 FY27.
- Net fixed-asset block rose only modestly, from ₹7.8 Cr (FY22) to ₹9.6 Cr (FY26/Q1 FY27), consistent with the asset-light operating model.
- Sanctioned fund-based working capital limits increased from ~₹31 Cr (FY22: SBI 16 + IDBI 5 + Kotak 10) to ~₹37 Cr (Q1 FY27: SBI 23.5 + IDBI 3.5 + ICICI 10) to fund higher business volumes.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Describes itself as a prominent global logistics firm offering freight forwarding, transportation and customs clearance, with 26+ years of industry experience, a nationwide presence, and exposure to Automotive, Renewable Energy, Engineering, Textiles, Commodities, Pharmaceuticals and FMCG sectors.
- Operates an Asset-Light Approach Model, partnering with players worldwide rather than owning transport assets, to deliver dependable, efficient and punctual cargo transportation; self-styled as 'Pioneering End-to-End Logistics Globally.'
- Q1 FY27 saw renewal of the logistics mandate with Bank Note Paper Mill India and a new break-bulk logistics contract from BHEL, which the CMD cited as reflecting 'the trust customers place in our execution capabilities.'
- Client base of 200+, but top-5 customer revenue concentration has run 46-84% over FY22-FY26 (46% in FY26, 50% in Q1 FY27), indicating a scaled yet still concentrated customer base.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Recognition] Multiple 2026 industry awards cited: 'Logistics Company of the Year' (All India Maritime and Logistics Awards 2026), 'Logistics Champion – Mid-Sized Company' (ISCM Logistics Ranking 2026), '25 Years of Logistics Excellence' (Conquest 2026), plus Great Place To Work certification (July 2024 to July 2025).
- [Promoter] Founded in 2000 by Chairman & MD Harpreet Singh Malhotra, a first-generation entrepreneur with prior international automotive-logistics experience, including bringing BMW motorcycles to India.

themes.title: Logistics, ports & supply-chain formalization
themes.need: E-commerce, quick-commerce and GST-driven warehousing consolidation plus a 1P->3P shift drive an integrated-logistics up-cycle. DELHIVERY hit early FCF (>1B parcels, Express +46% rev) with Express targeting 16-18% margin; CONCOR/GATEWAY/JSWINFRA on rail/ports; ALLCARGO/MAHLOG/TVSSCS/VRLLOG on 3PL/road; BLUEDART/TCIEXP/WCIL/SNOWMAN on express + cold-chain; DELHIVERY/SHADOWFAX on quick-commerce fulfilment. Q1FY27's clearest turnaround datapoint: MAHLOG swung to a +INR 25.4cr PAT from a -INR 10.8cr loss on +23% revenue, with B2B Express (Rivigo) gross margin turning +6% from -3.8% and its EBITDA loss cut to -INR 1.6cr from -INR 11.8cr, guided to EBITDA breakeven within FY27, while Contract Logistics grew 26% with margin diluted only ~46bps on new-site start-up costs (opening a site almost every week).
themes.driver: Express/quick-commerce volume momentum; warehousing leasing; port/rail throughput; operating-leverage inflection.
